title: ASCAT SSM CDR2014-EXT (DATA RECORDS H108)
abstract: This data provides surface soil moisture estimates derived from the Metop ASCAT instrument using a semi-empirical change detection method developed by TU Wien. Multi-angle backscatter observations from Metop ASCAT are used to generate relative surface soil moisture information, expressed as degree of saturation (0?100%). The product includes processing, correction, and confidence flags to indicate the quality of each retrieval. The H108 Metop ASCAT SSM CDR2014-EXT represents an extension of the H25 Metop ASCAT SSM CDR2014 product, using the same Level 1b input data, soil moisture retrieval algorithm, and empirical model parameters.

title: ASCAT SSM NRT 12.5 km (H29)
abstract: This data provides estimates of surface soil moisture derived from Advanced SCATterometer (ASCAT) backscatter observations. The product is given in swath orbit geometry with a 12.5 km sampling and represents the water content of the top 0?5 cm soil layer, expressed as a degree of saturation between 0 and 100%. Soil moisture is estimated using a linear relationship between backscatter and soil moisture, combined with change detection techniques to remove the contributions of vegetation, land cover, and surface topography, which are assumed invariant from year to year. Seasonal vegetation effects are modeled using ASCAT?s multi-angle viewing capabilities. The soil moisture processor was developed by Vienna University of Technology (TU Wien). Some data have been reprocessed; users should refer to associated product validation reports or release notes for details.

title: ASCAT25, OSI-102-b, OAS025
abstract: This data provides the ASCAT Multi-parameter product, which contains surface wind vectors over the ocean and a soil moisture index over land. The product also includes the backscatter values used in the retrieval of these geophysical parameters, along with several quality flags to support data usage. For numerical weather prediction (NWP) applications, the product is provided in BUFR format, while the netCDF version contains wind data only. Users interested in ASCAT backscatter, wind, or soil moisture index data in other formats should refer to the corresponding dedicated product entries. Although the OSI SAF is identified as the originating centre for this product, the processing of soil moisture index values is performed by EUMETSAT.

title: AU_Land
abstract: This dataset provides Level-2B soil moisture estimates from the Advanced Microwave Scanning Radiometer 2 (AMSR2) onboard the GCOM-W1 satellite. AMSR2 is a microwave radiometer that measures weak microwave emissions from the Earth's surface and atmosphere from an altitude of approximately 700 km, supporting applications in hydrology, agriculture, and climate studies. The AMSR2 antenna rotates once every 1.5 seconds, acquiring data over a 1450 km swath using a conical scan mechanism, which allows daytime and nighttime observations with >99% global coverage every 2 days. AMSR2 succeeds AMSR (ADEOS-II/Japan) and AMSR-E (Aqua/NASA). This AMSR-E/AMSR2 Unified Level-2B land product provides a long-term, consistent record by merging AMSR-E and AMSR2 observations. Surface soil moisture is derived from L1R brightness temperatures using the Normalized Polarization Difference (NPD) algorithm and the Single Channel Algorithm (SCA). Ancillary information is included, and all data are gridded onto the 25 km Equal-Area Scalable Earth Grid (EASE-Grid) for standardized spatial representation.

title: CLMS soil moisture
abstract: This data provides daily observations of Surface Soil Moisture (SSM) over continental Europe at a spatial resolution of 1 km, covering the period from October 2014 to the present. SSM represents the relative water content in the top few centimetres of soil, expressed in percent saturation, describing how wet or dry the soil is at the surface. The dataset is derived from satellite radar measurements, providing high-resolution information on local soil moisture conditions. The product is provided in raster format, with daily temporal frequency and global coverage limited to continental Europe, enabling consistent and detailed monitoring of surface soil moisture dynamics.

title: CYGNSS_L3_SOIL_MOISTURE_V1.0
abstract: The CYGNSS Level 3 Soil Moisture Product provides volumetric water content estimates for soils between 0-5 cm depth at a 6-hour discretization for most of the subtropics. The data were produced by CYGNSS investigators at the University Corporation for Atmospheric Research (UCAR) and the University Colorado at Boulder (CU), and derive from version 2.1 of the CYGNSS L1 SDR. The soil moisture algorithm uses collocated soil moisture retrievals from SMAP to calibrate CYGNSS observations from the same day. For a given location, a linear relationship between the SMAP soil moisture and CYGNSS reflectivity is determined and used to transform the CYGNSS observations into soil moisture. The data are archived in daily files in netCDF-4 format. Two soil moisture variables report the volumetric water content in units of cm3/cm3. The variable SM_subdaily includes up to four soil moisture estimates per day. Another variable SM_daily provides a daily average. The time series covers the period from March 2017 to present.

title: CYGNSS_L3_SOIL_MOISTURE_V3.2
abstract: The CYGNSS Level 3 Soil Moisture V3.2 dataset is provided by the CYGNSS Science Team of the University of Michigan. It estimates volumetric water content for soils between 0-5 cm depth at a 6-hour discretization for most of the subtropics from the V3.2 reflectivity measurements provided in the CYGNSS L1 SDR dataset (https://doi.org/10.5067/CYGNS-L1X32). CYGNSS was launched on 15 December 2016, it is a NASA Earth System Science Pathfinder Mission that was launched with the purpose of collecting the first frequent space?based measurements of surface wind speeds in the inner core of tropical cyclones. Originally made up of a constellation of eight micro-satellites, the observatories provide nearly gap-free Earth coverage using an orbital inclination of approximately 35° from the equator, with a mean (i.e., average) revisit time of seven hours and a median revisit time of three hours. The soil moisture retrieval algorithm is an update of the previous version developed by UCAR-CU using a linear regression of CYGNSS angle-normalized effective surface reflectivity trained against collocated SMAP soil moisture during the calibration period 8/1/2018 to 11/15/2023. The data are archived in daily files in netCDF-4 format. Volumetric soil moisture water content in units of cm3/cm3 is provided with two gridding resolutions, 9x9 km and 36x36 km. The variable SM_subdaily contains data reported in six hour intervals. The variable SM_daily provides a daily average. The time series covers the period from August 2018 to present.

title: LPRM_AMSR2_A_SOILM3
abstract: The AMSR2/GCOM-W1 Surface Soil Moisture L3 1-Day 25 km × 25 km Daytime V001 dataset is derived from observations by the Advanced Microwave Scanning Radiometer 2 (AMSR2) aboard the GCOM-W1 satellite. It provides daily gridded measurements of surface soil moisture, land surface temperature, and vegetation water content, retrieved using the Land Parameter Retrieval Model (LPRM) applied to AMSR2 brightness temperatures. Land surface temperature is independently estimated from the Ka-band (36.5 GHz) channel, while surface soil moisture and vegetation optical depth are obtained through a forward radiative transfer model. Each day includes separate ascending (daytime) and descending (nighttime) products, with this dataset representing the daytime passes. The temporal coverage begins in May 2012. Data are archived and distributed by the Goddard Earth Sciences Data and Information Services Center (GES DISC).

title: LPRM_AMSR2_DS_SOILM2
abstract: The AMSR2/GCOM-W1 Downscaled Surface Soil Moisture L2B V001 dataset is derived from observations by the Advanced Microwave Scanning Radiometer 2 (AMSR2) aboard the GCOM-W1 satellite. It provides swath-level measurements of surface soil moisture, land surface temperature, and vegetation water content, retrieved using the Land Parameter Retrieval Model (LPRM) applied to AMSR2 brightness temperatures. Land surface temperature is independently estimated from the Ka-band (36.5 GHz) channel, while surface soil moisture and vegetation optical depth are obtained through a forward radiative transfer model. The dataset spans from May 2012, when the GCOM-W1 satellite was launched, to the present. Its spatial resolution is derived by resampling AMSR2?s native C- and X-band resolutions (approximately 46 and 31 km) to 25 km × 25 km and further downscaling to 10 km × 10 km grids using the Smoothing Filter-based Intensity Modulation (SFIM) technique. Each swath includes corresponding geolocation fields. Data are archived and distributed by the Goddard Earth Sciences Data and Information Services Center (GES DISC).

abstract: This data provides global estimates of surface soil moisture based on combined model and satellite observations. The analysed soil moisture fields are derived from a modelled first guess, screen-level temperature and humidity analyses, and ASCAT-derived surface soil moisture. These fields are then re-scaled into a soil wetness index by normalizing with the saturated soil moisture value according to soil type. The global product is generated using input from the EUMETCast SSM (Surface Soil Moisture) product and is distributed for use in climate monitoring, hydrology studies, and agricultural applications.

abstract: This data provides daily observations of Volumetric soil moisture (m3/m3) over continental Europe at a spatial resolution of 1 km, covering the period from October 2014 to the present. The product is provided in raster format, with daily temporal frequency and global coverage limited to continental Europe, enabling consistent and detailed monitoring of surface soil moisture dynamics.

title: Soil_Moisture_cci: PASSIVE Product
abstract: This data provides the Soil Moisture CCI PASSIVE dataset, one of three datasets created as part of the European Space Agency's (ESA) Soil Moisture Essential Climate Variable (ECV) Climate Change Initiative (CCI) project. The PASSIVE product is generated by merging soil moisture retrievals from the SMMR, SSM/I, TMI, AMSR-E, WindSat, FY-3B, FY-3C, FY-3D, AMSR2, MIRAS (SMOS), GPM, and SMAP passive microwave instruments. The v09.1 PASSIVE dataset is provided as global daily images in NetCDF-4 classic file format, with a spatial resolution of 0.25 degrees. It contains surface soil moisture expressed in volumetric units [m³/m³] and covers the period 1978-11-01 to 2023-12-31. The dataset is supported by detailed documentation, including the Algorithm Theoretical Baseline Document and related references, which describe the theoretical background and processing methodology. Data were processed by the ESA CCI Soil Moisture project team and are distributed via the CEDA ESA CCI Open Data Portal.

title: SPL2SMAP_S
abstract: This dataset provides Level-2 soil moisture estimates derived from the NASA Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) mission, launched in 2015. SMAP carries both an active radar and a passive radiometer, enabling global measurements of soil moisture content and freeze/thaw state. The active radar transmits microwave pulses and measures backscatter, while the passive radiometer observes natural microwave emissions, providing complementary soil moisture observations. The Level-2 product combines SMAP L-band brightness temperatures with Copernicus Sentinel-1A and -1B C-band backscatter data. Soil moisture estimates are retrieved from both 6:00 a.m. descending and 6:00 p.m. ascending half-orbit passes and resampled to a 3 km Equal-Area Scalable Earth Grid, Version 2.0 (EASE-Grid 2.0). These data support applications in weather forecasting, agricultural monitoring, water resource management, and climate studies.

title: SPL2SMP_E
abstract: This dataset provides the enhanced Level-2 (L2) soil moisture product from the NASA Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) mission, launched in 2015. SMAP carries both an active radar and a passive radiometer to measure soil moisture content and freeze/thaw state, supporting applications in weather forecasting, agriculture, water resource management, and climate studies. The enhanced L2 product includes calibrated and geolocated brightness temperatures from the SMAP radiometer, collected during both 6:00 a.m. descending and 6:00 p.m. ascending half-orbit passes. Derived from Level-1B interpolated antenna temperatures, these data apply Backus-Gilbert optimal interpolation techniques to maximize information extraction and convert antenna temperatures into brightness temperatures. The resulting data are projected onto the 9 km Equal-Area Scalable Earth Grid, Version 2.0 (EASE-Grid 2.0) using a global cylindrical projection (available as the SPL1CTB_E product). Since 2021, data have also been distributed in the Northern Hemisphere EASE-Grid 2.0 with an azimuthal equal-area projection. These 9 km brightness temperatures form the basis for retrieving surface soil moisture estimates, distributed as the SPL2SMP_E product.

title: SPL2SMP_NRT
abstract: This dataset provides the Near Real-Time (NRT) Level-2 Radiometer Half-Orbit 36 km Soil Moisture product (SPL2SMP_NRT) from the NASA Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) mission, launched in 2015. SMAP carries both an active radar and a passive L-band radiometer to measure soil moisture content and freeze/thaw state, supporting applications in weather forecasting, agriculture, water resource management, and climate studies. The NRT product offers soil moisture estimates within three hours of satellite observation, using the latest available ancillary data and spacecraft/antenna attitude information to minimize latency. Data are provided for both ascending and descending half-orbit passes at 36 km resolution on the Equal-Area Scalable Earth Grid, Version 2.0 (EASE-Grid 2.0). The SMAP satellite achieves near-global coverage (86.4°S to 86.4°N) every 2?3 days, with swath widths of 1000 km. NRT data are retained for 2?3 weeks, giving users access to at least 14 consecutive days at any given time. While NRT products are intended for operational applications requiring low latency, users needing the highest quality data are encouraged to use the standard SPL2SMP product

title: SPL3SMP_E
abstract: This dataset provides Level-3 daily global soil moisture estimates from the NASA Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) mission, launched in 2015. SMAP is equipped with both an active radar and a passive radiometer to measure soil moisture content and freeze/thaw state, supporting applications in weather forecasting, agriculture, water resource management, and climate studies. The Level-3 product consolidates daily land surface conditions using observations from the SMAP radiometer. It is derived from Level-2 soil moisture products, which in turn use Level-1C interpolated brightness temperatures. Backus-Gilbert optimal interpolation techniques are applied to convert SMAP antenna temperatures into brightness temperatures, which are then projected onto the 9 km Equal- Area Scalable Earth Grid, Version 2.0 (EASE-Grid 2.0) in a global cylindrical projection. Since 2021, data are also available on the Northern Hemisphere EASE-Grid 2.0 using an azimuthal equal-area projection.

title: SPL4SMGP
abstract: This data provides global estimates of surface and root zone soil moisture through the SMAP Level-4 (L4) product suite, which consists of three complementary datasets. The SMAP L4 Global 3-hourly 9 km EASE-Grid Surface and Root Zone Soil Moisture Geophysical Data (SPL4SMGP, DOI: 10.5067/T5RUATAQREF8) contains 3-hourly time-averaged geophysical land surface fields and is the primary product for most users. The SMAP L4 Global 3-hourly 9 km EASE-Grid Soil Moisture Analysis Update (SPL4SMAU, DOI: 10.5067/02LGW4DGJYRX) provides diagnostic information from land surface analysis updates, including assimilated SMAP observations, model predictions, analysis estimates, and additional data assimilation diagnostics. The SMAP L4 Global 9 km EASE-Grid Soil Moisture Land Model Constants (SPL4SMLM, DOI: 10.5067/PXQIBL2ALDZD) supplies static, time-invariant land surface model constants required for further interpretation of the geophysical fields, and consists of a single file per product version. The L4_SM products are generated by assimilating SMAP L-band brightness temperature data from descending and ascending half-orbit passes (approximately 6:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m. local solar time) into a land surface model. This approach enhances soil moisture estimation by combining satellite observations with model physics, enabling the generation of temporally consistent soil moisture fields. The data are provided globally on the Equal-Area Scalable Earth Grid, Version 2.0 (EASE-Grid 2.0), at 9 km spatial resolution, with SPL4SMGP and SPL4SMAU available in 3-hourly intervals and SPL4SMLM as a static reference file. All products are distributed in NetCDF format. (2) SMAP L4 Global 3-hourly 9 km EASE-Grid Surface and Root Zone Soil Moisture Analysis Update (SPL4SMAU, DOI: 10.5067/LWJ6TF5SZRG3) (3) SMAP L4 Global 9 km EASE-Grid Surface and Root Zone Soil Moisture Land Model Constants (SPL4SMLM, DOI: 10.5067/KN96XNPZM4EG) For each product, SMAP L-band brightness temperature data from descending and ascending half-orbit satellite passes (approximately 6:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m. local solar time, respectively) are assimilated into a land surface model that is gridded using an Earth-fixed, global cylindrical 9 km Equal-Area Scalable Earth Grid, Version 2.0 (EASE-Grid 2.0) projection.

title: SSM ASCAT-A NRT O25 (H102)
abstract: This data provides estimates of surface soil moisture derived from Advanced SCATterometer (ASCAT) backscatter observations. The product is given in swath orbit geometry with a 25 km sampling and represents the water content of the top 0?5 cm soil layer, expressed as a degree of saturation between 0 and 100%. Soil moisture is estimated using a linear relationship between backscatter and soil moisture, combined with change detection techniques to remove the contributions of vegetation, land cover, and surface topography, which are assumed invariant from year to year. Seasonal vegetation effects are modeled using ASCAT?s multi-angle viewing capabilities. The soil moisture processor was developed by Vienna University of Technology (TU Wien). Some data have been reprocessed; users should refer to associated product validation reports or release notes for details.

title: ASCAT25, OSI-102, OSI-102-c, OSI-102-b, OAS025
abstract: This data provides the ASCAT Multi-parameter product, which contains surface wind vectors over the ocean and a soil moisture index over land. The product also includes the backscatter values used in retrieving these geophysical parameters, as well as several quality flags to support proper data usage. For numerical weather prediction (NWP) applications, the product is available in BUFR format, while the netCDF version contains wind data only. Users interested in ASCAT backscatter, wind, or soil moisture index data in other formats should refer to the corresponding dedicated product entries. Although the OSI SAF is listed as the originating centre, the processing of soil moisture index values is carried out by EUMETSAT. These data are available in the Data Centre beginning 28 February 2011. Archived near-real-time (NRT) data prior to that date may be requested from the OSI SAF helpdesk. For Metop-A, it is strongly recommended to use the reprocessed ASCAT winds data records (DOI: 10.15770/EUM_SAF_OSI_0006) instead of this archived NRT product for the period before 1 April 2014. Metop-A data are available in the Data Centre up to 15 November 2021.

title: SPL4SMAU
abstract: This data provides global estimates of surface and root zone soil moisture from the Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) mission, launched by NASA in 2015. SMAP carries both active and passive remote sensing instruments: the radar transmits microwave pulses and measures the backscatter signal to infer soil moisture levels, while the radiometer observes naturally emitted microwave radiation from the Earth?s surface to provide complementary soil moisture data. Together, these measurements support improved weather forecasting, agricultural monitoring, water resource management, and studies of Earth?s water cycle dynamics. The SMAP Level-4 (L4) surface and root zone soil moisture data are distributed in three products: SPL4SMGP (DOI: 10.5067/EVKPQZ4AFC4D) ? Global 3-hourly 9 km EASE-Grid geophysical soil moisture fields. SPL4SMAU (DOI: 10.5067/LWJ6TF5SZRG3) ? Global 3-hourly 9 km EASE-Grid analysis update files, containing assimilated SMAP observations, model predictions, and analysis estimates. SPL4SMLM (DOI: 10.5067/KN96XNPZM4EG) ? Global 9 km EASE-Grid static land model constants, required for further interpretation of the geophysical fields. All products are generated by assimilating SMAP L-band brightness temperature observations from descending and ascending half-orbit passes (approximately 6:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m. local solar time) into a land surface model. The data are provided globally on the Equal-Area Scalable Earth Grid, Version 2.0 (EASE-Grid 2.0) at 9 km spatial resolution and are distributed in NetCDF format.

title: MIR_CLF4RA
abstract: The Soil Moisture and Ocean Salinity (SMOS) mission, launched by the European Space Agency (ESA) in 2009, is designed to provide global observations of soil moisture over land and sea surface salinity over oceans. The mission is equipped with a unique L-band interferometric radiometer, the Microwave Imaging Radiometer using Aperture Synthesis (MIRAS), which measures multi-angular brightness temperatures at 1.4 GHz. These observations contribute to improving climate and weather modeling, water resource management, and our understanding of the Earth?s water and energy cycles. The L4SM RZSM is the daily product of root zone soil moisture (m3/m3) representative of the 0-1 m depth of the soil. The product contains also a quality index taking into account the presence of Radio Frequency Interference (RFI), low quality of retrieval of the input surface soil moisture, and a high fraction of non- nominal surfaces. Products from reprocessing RE07 are available for the period 01/2010 - 05/2021. Products from operational (OPER) processing are available since 06/2021. Reprocessed products and operational products are derived using the same algorithm and configuration, hence ensuring the temporal continuity.

title: ASCAT SSM CDR v5 EXT 12.5 km (DATA RECORDS H116)
abstract: This data provides surface soil moisture derived from ASCAT (Advanced Scatterometer) backscatter observations and is available on a fixed Earth grid with 12.5 km sampling in time series format. The product estimates the water content of the 0?5 cm topsoil layer, expressed as degree of saturation between 0% (dry) and 100% (fully saturated). The retrieval algorithm is based on a linear relationship between soil moisture and scatterometer backscatter and applies change detection techniques to minimize the influence of vegetation, land cover, and surface topography, which are assumed invariant from year to year. Seasonal vegetation effects are modelled using the multi-angle viewing capabilities of ASCAT. The algorithm was developed by the Vienna University of Technology (TU Wien). This product represents an extension of the Metop ASCAT Surface Soil Moisture Climate Data Record v5 at 12.5 km sampling.

abstract: This data provides daily observations of Volumetric soil moisture (m3/m3) over continental Europe at a spatial resolution of 1 km, covering the period from October 2014 to the present. The product is provided in raster format, with daily temporal frequency and global coverage limited to continental Europe, enabling consistent and detailed monitoring of surface soil moisture dynamics.
